paper_claim: The clean analytical cohort contains 180 main trials reconstructed from an audited 186-record lineage.
numerical_result: 174 main_unique + 6 main_valid_replacement = 180 main trials; 6 known-error records excluded; 186/186 triplets verified
statistical_evidence: Not an inferential claim
allowed_wording: An audited lineage produced 180 main trials while retaining six known-error records outside the analysis.
forbidden_wording: Six erroneous files were deleted or silently replaced.
limitation: Validity status depends on the documented user-confirmed 20260729/20260730 replacement decision.

paper_claim: The independent human experimental unit is the participant, not the trial or block.
numerical_result: 5 participants; 45 trials per mode; 9 trials per participant per mode
statistical_evidence: All efficacy contrasts are computed from five participant-level paired differences
allowed_wording: Inference was conducted at participant level (n=5).
forbidden_wording: The study had n=180 independent observations or n=45 independent blocks.
limitation: Repeated trials improve within-participant precision but do not increase the number of independent humans.

paper_claim: Nominal mode labels did not fully represent the interventions realized during the trials.
numerical_result: G activated before task start in 42/45 and before contact in 43/45 trials; F activated before its intended 0.20-s delay in 42/45 trials; E vision lock followed contact in 5/45 trials
statistical_evidence: Descriptive event audit; no hypothesis test required
allowed_wording: Nominal labels did not always correspond to the logged timing of the realized intervention.
forbidden_wording: All four modes were executed exactly as nominally specified.
limitation: The audit identifies timing and implementation deviations but does not estimate how each deviation changed an individual outcome.

paper_claim: G adaptation usually began before task start.
numerical_result: 42/45 before task start; median -0.3790 s
statistical_evidence: Descriptive count and median
allowed_wording: G adaptation was already active before task start in 42 of 45 trials.
forbidden_wording: G was a purely post-contact force-feedback condition.
limitation: Task-start timing is reconstructed on the experiment monotonic timeline.

paper_claim: G adaptation usually began before logged contact.
numerical_result: 43/45 before contact; median -1.2144 s; 2/45 at or after contact
statistical_evidence: Descriptive count and median
allowed_wording: G adaptation preceded logged contact in 43 of 45 trials.
forbidden_wording: G isolated contact-triggered force refinement.
limitation: Logged contact onset is threshold based and is not an independently instrumented ground-truth contact event.

paper_claim: The observed G pre-activation is consistent with raw-force gating, the fixed 1-N deadband, and initialization before baseline readiness.
supporting_metric: raw force and baseline-relative activation timing
numerical_result: 45/45 first activations had raw estimated force >1 N; 42/45 occurred before baseline ready
statistical_evidence: Mechanistic interpretation supported by audited code logic and log timing, not a randomized mechanism contrast
allowed_wording: The G pre-activation pattern is consistent with the logged raw-force threshold and initialization sequence.
forbidden_wording: Contact detection caused G activation or the causal contribution of each software feature was separately identified.
limitation: Several implementation features co-occurred, so their individual causal contributions cannot be separated.

paper_claim: The intended 0.20-s F gate was not realized in most F trials.
numerical_result: median 0.0533 s after contact; 42/45 activated before 0.20 s
statistical_evidence: Descriptive count and median; code audit identifies mixed time.time/perf_counter domains
allowed_wording: F activation occurred at a median of approximately 0.053 s after logged contact, with 42 of 45 trials earlier than the intended 0.20-s gate.
forbidden_wording: F faithfully implemented a 0.20-s post-contact delay.
limitation: Three later activations followed late vision locking and do not validate the intended gate.

paper_claim: Vision locking occurred after task start in E/F and was not pre-contact in every trial.
numerical_result: E: median +1.7408 s from task start and -0.7546 s from contact; 5/45 after contact. F: median +1.7520 s from task start and -0.9411 s from contact; 3/45 after contact
statistical_evidence: Descriptive count and median
allowed_wording: Vision locking generally preceded contact but occurred after contact in 5 E trials and 3 F trials.
forbidden_wording: Vision-based stiffness was configured before contact in every E and F trial.
limitation: Vision timing is logged, but the clean tables do not identify a separately randomized visual-information mechanism.

paper_claim: E was associated with lower participant-mean early excess-force impulse than A.
statistical_evidence: paired t p=0.0201; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.0633, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: E was associated with a lower participant-mean early excess-force impulse than A, with a consistent directional estimate but limited confirmatory strength.
forbidden_wording: E significantly reduced force under all analyses; vision caused the reduction.
limitation: Only five independent participants were observed; E is a bundled configuration and the study was not preregistered.

paper_claim: All five participant-level E-A impulse differences were negative.
numerical_result: 5/5 participants had E < A
statistical_evidence: The smallest possible two-sided exhaustive sign-flip p-value at n=5 is 0.0625
allowed_wording: All five observed participant means were directionally lower under E than A.
forbidden_wording: The effect is established for the target population.
limitation: Directional consistency in five participants does not substitute for population-level confirmation.

paper_claim: Initial peak force was also lower on average in E than A, but the evidence is sensitivity-test limited.
statistical_evidence: paired t p=0.0263; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted t p=0.0789 and exact/Wilcoxon p=0.2500
allowed_wording: Initial peak force showed a concordant directional E-A difference.
forbidden_wording: E significantly lowered peak force after multiplicity correction.
limitation: This is a secondary metric and shares the same n=5 and bundled-mode limitations.

paper_claim: E was associated with longer approach time than A.
numerical_result: mean difference +1.7805 s; 95% t-CI [1.5084, 2.0527]; 5/5 participants E > A
statistical_evidence: paired t p=5.40e-05; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.000162, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: E was accompanied by a longer participant-mean approach time than A.
forbidden_wording: Vision caused operators to slow down.
limitation: The timing difference may reflect operator behavior, mode order, vision timing, or bundled controller differences.

paper_claim: E was associated with longer total task time than A.
numerical_result: mean difference +1.2128 s; 95% t-CI [0.5741, 1.8514]; 5/5 participants E > A
statistical_evidence: paired t p=0.00620; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.0186, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: E was accompanied by a longer participant-mean total task time than A.
forbidden_wording: The safety gain was caused by a specific visual or stiffness mechanism.
limitation: The study cannot separate deliberate caution from controller- or order-related timing effects.

paper_claim: The joint E-A pattern is compatible with a safety-efficiency trade-off.
supporting_metric: impulse, approach time, and total task time
numerical_result: impulse -0.3489 N*s; approach +1.7805 s; total task +1.2128 s
statistical_evidence: Participant directions were consistent for all three outcomes; exact and Holm-adjusted evidence remains limited by n=5
allowed_wording: The observed E-A pattern is consistent with a safety-efficiency trade-off.
forbidden_wording: A causal trade-off mechanism was proven.
limitation: The outcomes are jointly descriptive and do not establish mediation or causal mechanism.

paper_claim: G showed only a small average impulse difference from A under its realized implementation.
statistical_evidence: paired t p=0.1708; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.3416, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: Under the realized G implementation, the average G-A impulse difference was small and its interval included zero.
forbidden_wording: Post-contact force feedback reduced force.
limitation: G was mostly active before task/contact and therefore cannot be interpreted as a pure post-contact intervention.

paper_claim: F showed no stable incremental impulse advantage over E under the realized implementation.
statistical_evidence: paired t p=0.6556; exact sign-flip p=0.6875; Wilcoxon p=0.8125; LOPO changed sign when P03 was omitted
allowed_wording: The realized F implementation showed no discernible incremental advantage over E in this dataset.
forbidden_wording: Force refinement is ineffective or F is equivalent to E.
limitation: The F timing gate was not implemented as intended and the interval is compatible with effects in either direction.

paper_claim: The F-G contrast is descriptive rather than a clean synergy test.
statistical_evidence: paired t p=0.0158; exact sign-flip p=0.0625; Wilcoxon p=0.0625; Holm-adjusted p: t=0.0633, sign-flip=0.2500, Wilcoxon=0.2500
allowed_wording: F and G differed descriptively under their realized implementations.
forbidden_wording: Visual-force synergy was significant or F outperformed G because of force refinement.
limitation: Both modes contain different bundled and mistimed interventions, so this contrast does not identify an interaction.

paper_claim: The direction of the E-A impulse estimate was not driven by one participant.
numerical_result: five LOPO estimates ranged from -0.4028 to -0.2860 N*s and all retained the full-sample direction
statistical_evidence: One LOPO t-CI crossed zero; LOPO is a stability diagnostic, not a replacement test
allowed_wording: The E-A direction persisted in all leave-one-participant-out analyses.
forbidden_wording: The result remained statistically significant in every LOPO analysis.
limitation: Only four participants remain in each LOPO subset, producing very imprecise intervals.

paper_claim: Logged success did not distinguish the modes in the clean dataset.
numerical_result: 180/180 trials met the clean software-log success definition; participant-level success=1.0 in every mode
statistical_evidence: No comparative inference is meaningful because there is no observed variation
allowed_wording: All 180 clean trials met the predefined software-log success criterion.
forbidden_wording: All physical manipulations were independently verified as successful.
limitation: Success is derived primarily from software event logs rather than independent task verification.

paper_claim: The four nominal modes do not constitute a strict realized 2x2 factorial experiment.
numerical_result: G pre-contact activation 43/45; F gate earlier than 0.20 s in 42/45; E/F vision lock after contact in 5/45 and 3/45
statistical_evidence: Design conclusion from combined implementation audit
allowed_wording: The modes are treated as bundled realized configurations rather than a strict 2x2 factorial manipulation.
forbidden_wording: The data identify independent main effects of vision and force refinement or their interaction.
limitation: Mode order and other bundled parameters further limit factorial interpretation.

paper_claim: Realized stiffness trajectories differed from nominal categorical labels.
statistical_evidence: Descriptive trajectory summary
allowed_wording: Logged stiffness trajectories provide the realized intervention record for each mode.
forbidden_wording: Each mode can be represented by one fixed nominal stiffness value.
limitation: Interpolated contact-aligned values summarize logged trajectories and do not independently validate actuator-level physical stiffness.
